config.title: Image Gallery

intro.title: Image Gallery
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build an interactive image gallery component. You will learn to manage a collection of images using React state, allowing you to display and cycle through them. The core concept is handling user events, like button clicks, to update the UI dynamically. You'll use TypeScript to define types for your images and React hooks like useState to manage the current image index. By the end, you'll have a functional gallery that responds to user interactions.
intro.usecase: Image galleries are fundamental UI components found across modern web applications, from e-commerce product displays and social media feeds to portfolio websites and content management dashboards. Developers implement galleries to showcase visual content in applications like Instagram's photo grid, Airbnb's property listings, or Adobe's creative asset libraries. These components require handling user interactions like selection, navigation, and filtering while maintaining responsive layouts. Mastering gallery implementation prepares you for building real features like media browsers, product catalogs, and interactive content displays that users encounter daily.

objectives: Apply TypeScript interfaces to define a structured type for image objects with required properties.
Implement a React functional component with TypeScript to serve as the main gallery container.
Use the useState hook to create and manage an array state variable for storing gallery images.
Apply array iteration with the map method to render each image object as a visual element.
Construct JSX elements with appropriate HTML attributes to display image thumbnails in a grid layout.
Utilize CSS classes and inline styles to control the visual presentation and responsiveness of the gallery.
Implement event handlers to manage user interactions like clicks on gallery images.
Execute conditional rendering to display different UI states based on component data or user actions.
Define and invoke helper functions to perform operations like filtering or sorting the image collection.
Use the useEffect hook to perform side effects such as loading initial image data from a mock source.
Apply prop drilling or context to pass data and functions between parent and child gallery components.
Return structured JSX that combines state, iteration, and conditional logic into a complete gallery interface.

steps.title: Import React and useState from 'react'
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of importing React and useState
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.seedCode: // Import React and useState from 'react' here
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported, making them available for use in the component.
successCriteria: The code should have a valid import statement that imports both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and useState. This gives you access to React's core functionality and the useState hook for managing state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your import statement. Make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. You need to import both React and useState from the 'react' package using the import statement.

steps.title: Create the ImageGallery component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component called ImageGallery that returns JSX. The component should be defined after the imports.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or arrow function. Make sure it returns JSX (like a div or fragment).
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the ImageGallery component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named ImageGallery is defined and returns JSX.
successCriteria: The component is named ImageGallery, uses correct TypeScript syntax, and returns valid JSX.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the ImageGallery component. This is the main container for our gallery.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Is the component named exactly 'ImageGallery'? Does it return JSX?
steps.feedbackWrong: The component wasn't created correctly. Make sure to define a function or arrow function named ImageGallery that returns JSX.

steps.title: Define the image data type
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript interface called ImageItem with three properties: id (number), title (string), and url (string). Place this interface definition above the ImageGallery component.
steps.hint: Use the 'interface' keyword followed by the interface name and property definitions inside curly braces.
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have an ImageItem interface with the correct property types defined.
successCriteria: The interface must be named ImageItem and include id: number, title: string, and url: string properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the ImageItem interface with proper TypeScript types. This will ensure type safety when working with image data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that all three properties (id, title, url) are included with the correct TypeScript types (number for id, string for title and url).
steps.feedbackWrong: The interface definition is missing or incorrect. Make sure to use the 'interface' keyword, name it ImageItem, and include all three properties with their types.

steps.title: Initialize the images array
steps.instruction: Inside the ImageGallery component, create a constant named 'images' that is an array of ImageItem objects. Initialize it with at least two sample image objects, each having id, title, and url properties with appropriate values.
steps.hint: Use the ImageItem interface you defined earlier to type the array. Create sample objects like { id: 1, title: 'Mountain', url: 'https://example.com/mountain.jpg' }.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a typed images array with sample data that can be used for rendering.
successCriteria: Array is typed as ImageItem[] or Array<ImageItem>
Array contains at least two sample objects
Each object has id, title, and url properties with appropriate values
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a typed images array with sample data. This gives us real content to work with in the gallery.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: Did you type the array as ImageItem[]? Does it have at least two sample objects with id, title, and url properties?
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. Create a constant named 'images' inside the component. Make it an array of ImageItem objects with at least two sample images, each with id, title, and url properties.

steps.title: Initialize selectedImage state
steps.instruction: Inside your ImageGallery component, create a state variable called selectedImage using useState. Initialize it with null to represent that no image is selected initially.
steps.hint: Use the useState hook you imported earlier. The state should be typed to hold either an ImageItem object or null.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example of initializing a state variable with null
const [selectedItem, setSelectedItem] = useState<ItemType | null>(null);
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a selectedImage state variable initialized to null, ready to track which image is currently selected.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the selectedImage state variable. This will allow you to track which image the user has selected in the gallery.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've: 1) Used useState, 2) Named the variable 'selectedImage', 3) Initialized it to null, and 4) Properly typed it as ImageItem | null.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to create a state variable called selectedImage using useState, initialized to null, with the type ImageItem | null.

steps.title: Define the handleImageClick handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleImageClick inside your component. It should take one parameter of type ImageItem and call setSelectedImage with that parameter.
steps.hint: Create a function that accepts an ImageItem and updates the selectedImage state using the setter function.
steps.expectedOutcome: A properly typed click handler function that will be used to update the selected image when an image is clicked.
successCriteria: The function should be named handleImageClick, accept an ImageItem parameter, and call setSelectedImage with that parameter.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a properly typed click handler function that will update the selected image state.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your function accepts an ImageItem parameter and calls setSelectedImage with it.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function doesn't match the requirements. It should be named handleImageClick, accept an ImageItem parameter, and call setSelectedImage with that parameter.

steps.title: Define the handleCloseModal handler
steps.instruction: Define a function named handleCloseModal that sets the selectedImage state to null.
steps.hint: Create a function that calls setSelectedImage with null as the argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleCloseModal function is added that will clear the selected image when called.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've defined the handleCloseModal function correctly. This handler will be used to close the modal by clearing the selected image.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that your function calls setSelectedImage with null as the argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function should be named handleCloseModal and should call setSelectedImage(null).

steps.title: Return the main container div
steps.instruction: Update the return statement to wrap the existing <h1> element inside a <div> with className 'gallery-container'.
steps.hint: Add a <div> element around the existing content and give it the className attribute with value 'gallery-container'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component returns a <div> with className 'gallery-container' containing the <h1> element.
successCriteria: The return statement includes a <div> element
The <div> has className attribute set to 'gallery-container'
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully wrapped the gallery content in a container div with the appropriate className.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a <div> with className 'gallery-container' around the existing <h1> element.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement should include a <div> with className 'gallery-container' containing the <h1> element.

steps.title: Add the gallery title
steps.instruction: Inside the main container div, add an h1 element with the text 'Image Gallery'.
steps.hint:
Add

Image Gallery

inside the existing div.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a title inside a container

My Gallery
steps.expectedOutcome: The component renders a heading with the text 'Image Gallery'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the gallery title. The h1 element will display 'Image Gallery' at the top of your component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added an h1 element with the exact text 'Image Gallery' inside the main container div.
steps.feedbackWrong: The title isn't quite right. You need to add an h1 element with the text 'Image Gallery' inside the existing div.

steps.title: Create the images grid container
steps.instruction: Inside the component's return statement, after the gallery title, add a <div> element with the className 'gallery-grid' to serve as the container for the image thumbnails.
steps.hint: Add a div element with the className attribute set to 'gallery-grid'. This will be the parent container for the image thumbnails you'll add later.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a container div with the class 'gallery-grid' ready to hold image thumbnails.
successCriteria: A div element is added after the h1
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the gallery-grid container. This will hold the image thumbnails in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've added a div element with exactly className='gallery-grid' after the gallery title.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's focus on adding just the container div. Add a <div> element with className='gallery-grid' inside the main container, right after the <h1> element.

steps.title: Map through images and render thumbnails
steps.instruction: Inside the gallery-grid container div, map through the images array and render each item as an img element. Set the src attribute to the image's url, alt to its title, and wire the onClick event to call handleImageClick with the current image.
steps.hint: Use the map method on the images array. For each image, return an img element with the appropriate attributes.
steps.expectedOutcome: The gallery-grid container will contain img elements for each image in the images array, each clickable via handleImageClick.
successCriteria: Provide a key prop using image.id
Render an img element for each image
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully mapped through the images array and rendered clickable thumbnails. Each image now displays and is ready to trigger the click handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're mapping through the images array, providing a unique key for each item, and wiring the onClick to handleImageClick with the current image.
steps.feedbackWrong: The gallery-grid container should contain img elements generated by mapping the images array. Check that you're using images.map(), providing a key, and setting src, alt, and onClick correctly.

steps.title: Add conditional modal for selected image
steps.instruction: Add conditional rendering after the gallery grid that shows a modal when selectedImage is not null. The modal should contain the selected image's title and URL, and a close button wired to handleCloseModal.
steps.hint: Use a ternary operator or logical && to conditionally render JSX. The modal can be a simple div with a backdrop and content area.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will conditionally display a modal with the selected image's details when an image is clicked, and the modal can be closed with a button.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional rendering for the modal. The modal will appear when an image is selected and disappear when closed.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check: 1) Are you using selectedImage in the condition? 2) Does the modal show both title and URL? 3) Is the close button wired to handleCloseModal?
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's review conditional rendering. You need to add JSX after the gallery grid that only renders when selectedImage is not null, displaying the image details and a close button.
